summary.text: Pack ice is drift ice that has been driven together into one large mass covering more than 70% of the area.
Because drift ice is not attached to the shore or any fixed object, winds and sea currents carry it along and can pile it into ridges up to dozens of metres thick.
The two major packs, in the Arctic and Antarctic, change size a great deal with the seasons and have a significant impact on global changes in climate.

facts.label: Major packs
facts.value: The Arctic ice pack and the Antarctic ice pack

items.prompt: A harbour on a cold coast builds its pier so the end can be removed each winter. What is the main reason?

options.label: Heavy snow would make it collapse
Drifting ice rammed against it could shear it off
Fewer boats use the harbour in winter
Icebreakers need room to turn around

items.explain: Drift ice can exert huge forces on structures anchored to the shore, so they must be retractable or removable.

items.prompt: What turns scattered pieces of drifting sea ice into a pack?

options.label: They freeze onto the shoreline
They grow thicker than one metre
They are crowded into one dense mass
They break away from a glacier

items.explain: When drift ice is driven together into a large single mass with more than 70% coverage, it is called pack ice.

items.prompt: Out on a frozen polar sea stands a ridge of ice many metres thick. What most likely built it?

options.label: Snow piling up over many years
A glacier sliding off the land
Seawater freezing upward from below
Wind and currents piling up ice

items.explain: Wind and currents can push drift ice together into ridges up to dozens of metres thick.

items.prompt: Where is the southernmost place in the Northern Hemisphere where drifting sea ice can be seen?

options.label: The Sea of Okhotsk off northern Japan
The Baltic Sea off Denmark
The North Sea off Scotland
Hudson Bay in northern Canada

items.explain: The Sea of Okhotsk, by the northern coast of Hokkaidō, is the southernmost area in the Northern Hemisphere with drift ice.

items.prompt: How does the Arctic ice pack behave over the course of a year?

options.label: It stays about the same size all year
It drifts south until it reaches the tropics
It grows and shrinks a lot with the seasons
It only grows, adding ice every year

items.explain: Polar ice packs change their size significantly as the seasons change.

items.prompt: In one bay, a sheet of ice is frozen to the shore while another floats free nearby. A strong wind blows out to sea. Which sheet moves?

options.label: Only the sheet frozen to the shore
Only the free-floating sheet
Both move at the same speed
Neither, since wind cannot move ice

items.explain: Fast ice is fastened to a fixed object, while drift ice is carried along by winds and currents.
